subject: Hosted inference circuit-breaker triggered — temporary fallback and next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: James Nolan <james.nolan@lakestone.com>, ops@lakestone.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference circuit-breaker triggered — temporary fallback and next steps

Hi James / LakeStone ops team,

Quick note to let you know we observed an automated circuit-breaker trip against your hosted inference pool at ~09:06 PT. Traffic directed at your API keys began hitting elevated retry/backpressure conditions and to protect downstream latency SLOs our runtime applied a temporary fallback to the lower-capacity model variant for ~18 minutes while we assessed health. You may have seen a small uptick in 5xx/generic errors and a small change in response characteristics for a few requests.

What we know so far:
- Trigger time: 09:06 PT (automated circuit-breaker)
- Effect: incoming requests routed to model-variant v2026-03-quantized-fallback for ~09:06–09:24
- Observable impact: ~2–5% of requests experienced transient errors; tail latency increased for a subset of longer sequences

Immediate actions we took:
- Performed automatic fallback to the compatible model variant to protect latency SLOs
- Scaled an additional dedicated worker pool and purged a set of queued requests with corrupted KV state
- Opened incident INC-2026-0418-03 and PagerDuty PD-87654 (link below)

Next steps we will pursue in the next 6 hours:
1) Root-cause trace collection (we've attached initial kernel trace and runbook).
2) If needed, roll a targeted kernel recalibration and KV-cache refresh for LakeStone’s pool.
3) We'll provide a status-page update at T+1h and an ops summary at T+6h.

Action for LakeStone: if you can share any abnormal traffic patterns (bulk replay jobs, long-sequence bursts, retries) that started between 08:30–09:10 PT, please attach them here or to the Ops ticket.

Status links: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-2026-0418-03
PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-87654

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize a quality-preserving fix and a small credit to offset the spike in errors.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf), circuit_breaker-trace-20260418.txt (text)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted inference circuit-breaker triggered — temporary fallback and next steps

Eve — quick internal sync.

Brief notes from CS side after an initial pass on customer logs (James + Priya):
- LakeStone saw ~1400 requests between 08:50–09:05 that contained 3 very large batched documents (avg token length ~4200). The requests retried on 429s from their client for ~3 retries.
- Client retry pattern amplified the KV-cache pressure and contributed to slower token-serving tails.

Ops asks:
- Markus: can we confirm whether the KV-cache purge targeted LakeStone’s pool or was global? If global, need rollback plan.
- Ben: I looped Sales for the account impact and to prep comms; aim for one status update to customer at T+1h and a follow-up with credits once RCA available.

I can join an ops bridge if needed.

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: James Nolan <james.nolan@lakestone.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@lakestone.com>, ops@lakestone.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted inference circuit-breaker triggered — temporary fallback and next steps

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Evelyn.

We did start a large batched ingest at ~08:48 to warm a new customer index; the team thought it would be throttled but apparently the client retried heavily after a 429. We're pulling the client logs now and will attach a snippet.

Two immediate asks from our side:
1) Any temporary mitigation you can apply so we don't hit the fallback on subsequent ingest jobs this afternoon?
2) Rough ETA on a detailed timeline for the RCA — our engineering leadership will want to know cause and fix cadence.

Appreciate the offer for credits — we will coordinate billing contact after the RCA.

—James
Director of Platform Engineering
LakeStone Systems
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted inference circuit-breaker triggered — temporary fallback and next steps

Quick ops update:
- KV-cache purge was scoped to the LakeStone worker set; it was not global. We purged 3 worker shards that reported corrupt KV pointers.
- We applied a temporary soft-rate-limit override on LakeStone’s pool to reduce aggressive client retries from renewing capacity immediately; this should reduce repeat fallback triggers.
- Collected kernel traces and a request-level timeline; artifacts uploaded to INC ticket.

Planned: run a focused kernel recalibration tonight (low-traffic window) and validate with a small client-replay job (non-production). If results look good we will push the recalibration to the pool at 02:00 PT Sunday.

I'll post concise follow-ups on the incident ticket and set an ops-bridge recording.

—Markus
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: James Nolan <james.nolan@lakestone.com>, ops@lakestone.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: [Resolved] Incident INC-2026-0418-03 — summary and next steps

Hi James / LakeStone team,

Follow-up to confirm the incident is resolved and to summarize actions taken.

Incident summary:
- Root cause: a burst of large batched requests with aggressive client-side retries caused localized KV-cache pointer corruption on three LakeStone worker shards, leading the runtime to trigger the circuit-breaker and fall back to a compatible, lower-capacity model variant.
- Impact window: 09:06–09:24 PT on 2026-04-18; ~2–5% of requests experienced transient errors or altered response characteristics.

What we did:
- Scoped KV-cache purge to affected shards; applied a soft-rate-limit override to prevent retry storms from retriggering fallback.
- Ran a kernel recalibration in a low-traffic window and validated with a controlled replay.
- Restored primary model variant to LakeStone’s pool at 02:18 PT on 2026-04-19.

Customer-facing remedies:
- A credit will be issued for the error window; Ben, please coordinate with LakeStone’s billing contact.
- We recommend adding exponential backoff and jitter to client retries to avoid amplification.

Follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- RCA doc (Markus) — draft by 2026-04-21
- Postmortem and corrective actions (Eve / Ops / CS) — final by 2026-04-25

If you want a brief walk-through of the RCA once the draft is ready, we can schedule a 30-minute call. Thanks for your patience and for sharing the logs — that made diagnosing the retry amplification much faster.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
